findings.finding: Stable v0.5 process_episode stores pending activation/action state, while learn_outcome reuses those pending identities through predictor.observe and action_policy.reward without consuming or clearing them. The predictor increments the event count once per call and the action policy adds learning_rate*reward once per call.

findings.finding: Experience replay has been an established reinforcement-learning mechanism since Lin 1992; later prioritized replay explicitly reuses selected past transitions more frequently.
sources: Schaul et al., ICLR 2016, Prioritized Experience Replay

findings.finding: Replay ratio/update-to-data ratio is a fundamental algorithmic resource: changing the number of learning updates per experience materially changes performance in modern RL studies.
sources: Fedus et al., ICML 2020, Revisiting Fundamentals of Experience Replay

findings.finding: Prioritized replay treats replay frequency as deliberate sample weighting, with importance-sampling correction used when compensating for nonuniform sampling bias.
sources: Schaul et al., ICLR 2016, Prioritized Experience Replay

findings.finding: Human/animal neural replay is defined around sequential reactivation of neural patterns linked to past events during offline periods; repeated reward application to unchanged pending state without internal reactivation is not equivalent to biological replay.
sources: Zhang, Ou & Liu, Annual Review of Neuroscience 48 (2025), DOI 10.1146/annurev-neuro-112723-024516

findings.finding: A positive fixed timeshift result would be strongly reduced to implicit experience reuse/sample reweighting plus an outcome-consumption API policy. Future comparisons should match update-to-data ratio, and biological replay claims should require an actual internally reactivated state or sequence.
